clue.text: Opened up an alfresco feast

parts.note: alfresco means in the open air, i.e. out of doors
a spread is a lavish meal laid out

explanation.surface: Someone unpacks an open-air banquet for a picnic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread out wide has been opened up, as wings or a map are unfolded fully.

clue.text: Foreign character, part of a fearsome gang

indicators.note: part of tells you the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A mysterious foreigner belongs to a frightening gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but it means a letter of an alphabet, here a Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a symbol from a non-English script.

clue.text: Goes quiet — it's due to the old kitchen equipment

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone falls silent, blaming the antique cooking gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes quiet' reads as one phrase, but splits: goes are turns and quiet is the music abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnspits were rotating devices, or servants or dogs, that turned meat roasting over an open fire in historic kitchens.

clue.text: Left surrounded by rustics, make some quip

indicators.note: surrounded by means enclosed by the following word

parts.note: the peasantry are country folk collectively
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned among country folk tries a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light joking remark or witty comment made in conversation.

clue.text: A theologian taking ages over a piece of music

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first word above the second

parts.note: eras are long periods of time
MUS is the standard abbreviation for music, a piece of the word

explanation.surface: A scholar of divinity spends ages on one composition.
explanation.walkthrough: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the great Dutch Renaissance humanist and theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus was a renowned Dutch scholar who wrote on Christian doctrine and edited the Greek New Testament.

clue.text: Grandee's letters fomenting disorder

indicators.note: fomenting means stirring up trouble, so the letters are agitated

parts.note: the letters of the word

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's correspondence stirs up unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' looks like a noun but is the verb, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into confusion or upset the normal arrangement of things.

clue.text: Game may be caught by a man with craft

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Rudolf Hess, the Nazi deputy who flew a plane alone to Scotland in 1941

explanation.surface: A game might be snared by a crafty, cunning man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests cunning, but here it means an aircraft: Rudolf Hess famously piloted one to Scotland on a peace mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game for two players moving kings, queens and pawns.

clue.text: Many refuse ready money

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, a large number
ash is burnt waste

explanation.surface: Plenty of people turn down available funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb to decline, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is coins and notes on hand rather than credit, which is what people mean by notes and coins.

clue.text: An order incorrectly cited

indicators.note: wrongly set out, so the letters need putting right

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A command has been quoted wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or proclamation issued by someone in authority.

clue.text: Dull-coloured flag, say, never raised

parts.note: to flag is to droop or weaken
e.g., for example

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word reads upwards

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: A drab banner that, for example, was never hoisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but it is the verb meaning to droop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage green is a muted greyish green like the herb's leaves, a subdued, drab shade.

clue.text: Awesome oriental lake

parts.note: E for East, the oriental direction
Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A description of an Eastern lake that inspires wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense awesome means inspiring dread or fear, which is what something uncanny and unsettling does.

clue.text: Unusual police function

definitions.meaning: first meaning: striking, catching the attention
second meaning: taking a suspect into custody

explanation.surface: An odd duty assigned to the constabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking, remarkable sight stops you in your tracks; officers also detain suspects, which is literally the same word.

clue.text: Mugs people in the street — a charge results

parts.note: mugs are gullible fools, as are asses

indicators.note: one item sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for street
men as people in general

explanation.surface: Street muggings lead to criminal charges being laid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mugs' looks like a verb for street robbery, but it is a noun for dupes, and the people go inside the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a levy or tax charged on property or income, as in a rates assessment.

clue.text: A beast, though not with women

definitions.meaning: second meaning: for men only, as a pre-wedding party

explanation.surface: Someone is a brute, but at least not in female company.
explanation.definitionFit: The male deer is one sense; the adjective for a men-only gathering, like a bachelor party, is the other.

clue.text: See, not for the first time, about underworld protection

definitions.text: See, not for the first time

parts.note: re means concerning
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
cover is shelter or insurance

explanation.surface: Someone notices again a racket offering gangland protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld protection' suggests a criminal racket, but Dis is the classical land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something again after it was lost or forgotten is to come upon it a second time.

clue.text: "The wretched have no ____ ", or so wrote Dryden

definitions.text: "The wretched have no ____ ", or so wrote Dryden

parts.note: surface: a gap in a line of verse to be completed
setter's reading: recall the word John Dryden used for companions the unfortunate lack

explanation.surface: A quotation from the poet John Dryden with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the line comes from Dryden's play All for Love.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word names the companions and allies who desert people fallen on misfortune, completing the poet's line.

clue.text: Anticipatory — like television viewers!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: tele- is Greek for far and vision is seeing, so viewers see far

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal translation of television from its Greek and Latin roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with foresight plans ahead wisely; the word also literally describes seeing at a great distance.

clue.text: Stand with outstretched arms on the dinner table!

definitions.text: Stand with outstretched arms on the dinner table!

parts.note: surface: a person standing up with arms spread wide
setter's reading: an ornamental branched centrepiece whose arms hold dishes of fruit or sweets

explanation.surface: Someone climbs onto the dinner table and spreads their arms wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' reads as a verb for a person, but it is a noun: a display stand whose branches are its arms.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is a decorative table centrepiece with several branching holders for fruit, flowers or sweetmeats.

clue.text: A sound man, having some pluck

definitions.text: A sound man, having some pluck

parts.words: A sound man, having some pluck
parts.note: surface: a reliable, courageous fellow
setter's reading: a man making musical sound by plucking strings

explanation.surface: Praise for a dependable chap with a bit of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' means dependable and 'pluck' bravery on the surface; really the man makes sound and plucks strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays a fretted stringed instrument by plucking or strumming produces musical sound.

clue.text: Book put by for a rainy day?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to arrange in advance, as a table

definitions.text: put by for a rainy day
definitions.meaning: second meaning: savings kept back for emergencies

explanation.surface: A book set aside to read when the weather turns bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a noun for a volume, but it is the verb meaning to arrange in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a seat is to secure it ahead; a stock of funds kept back for emergencies is also called this.

clue.text: The cost of installing coops in a river

indicators.note: installing means putting one thing within another

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
pens are enclosures for animals

explanation.surface: A farmer ponders what it costs to set up hen coops in a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Expense is the money spent or outlay required to pay for something.

clue.text: Out — in — out: it can be good training

indicators.note: the second out means put out of order, so the letters before it get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drilling a sequence like a hokey-cokey dance step makes for good practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Out' is fodder and the second is the signal; the letters of out, in and it make up the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is instruction or teaching given to a pupil, the act of educating someone in a skill.

clue.text: Great rush to hire outside right

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around the following letter

parts.note: to rent is to hire
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: There is a scramble to hire something just outside the right side.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent, fast-flowing stream of water, or any overwhelming outpouring.

clue.text: Looked over a newspaper leader about the demode

indicators.note: about here means around, so one part wraps the other

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the person who heads a newspaper
ye is the old-fashioned form of 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone read through an editorial on what is out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests an editorial article, but it is the person in charge. Demode means out of date, so the old-style 'the' is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To have eyed something is to have looked it over, scrutinising it carefully.

clue.text: Follow directions — and then use wrongly

parts.note: E and N, east and north, two compass directions
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions are obeyed, then misapplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow directions' reads as one phrase, but 'Follow' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards or result from something, coming next in sequence.

clue.text: Take account of rise in value

definitions.meaning: first meaning: recognise, be fully aware of
second meaning: to gain worth, as property does

explanation.surface: Factor in an investment gaining worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To be grateful for or recognise something is one sense; assets gaining financial worth over time is the other.

clue.text: Odds, oddly enough

parts.note: surface: betting prices
setter's reading: the betting price is named after the opposite of odd numbers

explanation.walkthrough: A bet at one-to-one is quoted by a word meaning the opposite of odd, which is the irony the clue enjoys.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a one-to-one price where the stake is doubled if successful is called by this name.

clue.text: A residence that lowers the tone?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the musical sign lowering a note by a semitone

explanation.surface: A home that drags down the neighbourhood's standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers the tone' is an idiom for cheapening a place, but here it is literal: the musical symbol drops pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment on one floor of a building is one sense; the music symbol lowering pitch by a semitone is the other.

clue.text: Silence on changes effected — such boldness!

indicators.note: making changes to the preceding words means rearranging their letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone imposes silence and makes changes, and the cheek of it causes outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolence is rude, disrespectful cheek, a brazen form of audacity towards others.

clue.text: Say there's nothing in immorality

indicators.note: one thing in another means it goes inside

parts.note: vice is wickedness
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A claim that wickedness contains nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like the start of a sentence, but it is the noun: having a say means having a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a say in a matter is to have a voice, the right to express an opinion.

clue.text: Commanding gun carrying soldiers

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one part surrounds the other

parts.note: gat is old slang for a pistol
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A soldier in command carries a firearm among the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A commanding figure is imposing and dominant, much like a grand or eminent person.

clue.text: An illness that can excite interest about one

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A disease that stirs curiosity in someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteritis is inflammation of the intestine, a medical disorder often causing diarrhoea.
